## Required Library
```r
# seq() is part of base R — no package installation needed
```

## Syntax

```r
seq(from, to)
seq(from, to, by = step)
seq(from, to, length.out = n)
```
::: {.desc-item}
`seq()` creates a numeric sequence from a start value to an end value.
You can control the spacing with `by`, or request a fixed number of values with `length.out`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## When should you use `seq()`?
Use `seq()` whenever you need evenly spaced numeric values.
Common uses include time vectors, concentration grids, and x-values for plotting smooth curves.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## `seq()` vs `:`
The `:` operator is quick for simple integer steps like `1:10`.
Use `seq()` when you need decimal steps, a fixed output length, or descending sequences with custom step size.
:::

## Examples

<div class="example-section">
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Create a basic integer sequence</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
seq(1, 10)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Set a custom step size with <code>by</code></summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
seq(0, 2, by = 0.25)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Generate a fixed number of values with <code>length.out</code></summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
seq(0.1, 100, length.out = 8)
```
</div>
</details>

<details class="example-item">
<summary>Create a descending sequence</summary>
<div class="example-body">

```{webr}
seq(10, 0, by = -2)
```
</div>
</details>

</div>

## Argument Overview
<p class="arg-intro">Required arguments must be included when using a function while optional arguments can be included on demand.</p>

::: {.arg-section}
<div class="collapse-toolbar"><button class="collapse-btn">Expand All</button></div>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>from</code> — start value <span class="arg-types">numeric</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
The first value in the sequence.

```r
seq(from = 0, to = 1, by = 0.2)
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> <code>numeric</code></p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>to</code> — end value <span class="arg-types">numeric</span> <span class="arg-badge required">Required</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
The target end value of the sequence.

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> <code>numeric</code></p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>by</code> — step size <span class="arg-types">numeric</span> <span class="arg-badge optional">Optional</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
Difference between consecutive values.
Use a negative value for descending sequences.

```r
seq(10, 0, by = -2)
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> <code>numeric</code></p>
</div>
</details>

<details class="arg-item">
<summary><code>length.out</code> — number of output values <span class="arg-types">integer</span> <span class="arg-badge optional">Optional</span></summary>
<div class="arg-body">
Creates exactly this many values between `from` and `to`.

```r
seq(0, 1, length.out = 6)
```

<p class="data-types"><strong>Data Types:</strong> <code>integer</code></p>
</div>
</details>
:::
